name: s03-dunder
title: Syntax calls special methods
spec: A two-column mapping, five rows, left column what you write in monospace, right column the special method Python calls in monospace, joined by a short arrow in each row: len(x) -> x.__len__() ; x[i] -> x.__getitem__(i) ; x + y -> x.__add__(y) ; for item in x -> x.__iter__() ; with x -> x.__enter__() and x.__exit__(). Bottom green bar: implement the method and your class works with the built-in syntax.
cap: The data model: everyday syntax is a call to a special method on your object.

name: s03-ctxmgr
title: What a with block guarantees
spec: A vertical timeline of three boxes with arrows: 1 __enter__ runs and its result is bound by as ; 2 the body of the with block runs ; 3 __exit__ runs, even if the body raised an error (orange). Left side a small code chip: with resource as r:
cap: A context manager: __exit__ always runs, even when the body raises.

name: s03-closure
title: A closure remembers its variables
spec: Left box make_averager() with a local list series. Arrow labelled returns to the middle box averager (inner function). A dotted line from averager to a small green cell box labelled series (free variable, kept alive). Right: three calls averager(10), averager(11), averager(12) with results 10.0, 10.5, 11.0. Orange note: the state survives after make_averager returns.
alt: A closure keeps its free variable
cap: A closure: the inner function keeps the variable it uses from the enclosing function alive between calls.

name: s03-pipeline
title: A lazy generator pipeline
spec: A horizontal pipeline of four boxes joined by arrows: read lines (generator) ; filter lines (generator) ; parse fields (generator) ; sum (consumer, orange). Under the arrows a note: one item at a time flows through all stages. Under the pipeline a green bar: memory stays flat however large the file is.
cap: A generator pipeline: each stage pulls one item at a time from the stage before it, so memory stays flat.
